title: Ford’s new AI assistant can check your fuel levels and tire pressure
slides: Can Ford's AI assistant actually trust your tires?
It reads fuel and pressure directly from sensors
But it fails silently when sensors malfunction
You must verify alerts manually before driving
Test it today: ignore one alert and observe
thread_text:
1. Your tires are lying to you

The Ford AI assistant reads tire pressure and fuel directly from sensors, but it doesn't tell you when those sensors are lying. You could be driving on a warning that means nothing, or missing one that means everything.

2. The silent failure problem

When a sensor malfunctions, the AI doesn't warn you — it just quietly uses the bad data. You'd never know unless you independently check every reading before hitting the road.

3. Manual verification is the rule

Ford's system expects you to double-check all alerts manually — even the ones it flags as urgent. That's not an assistant; that's a notifier with a badge.

4. The trust paradox

If you trust the AI too much, you risk driving on unsafe tires. If you trust it too little, you're back to doing all the work yourself. The tool only works if you never fully rely on it.

5. Try this test this week

Ignore one of its tire alerts on your next drive. See if the AI notices it ignored or just carries on. That'll show you how much you can really trust it.

instagram.caption:
Your tires can lie to you, and Ford’s new AI assistant won’t catch it.  

It reads fuel levels and tire pressure straight from the sensors, but when a sensor fails, it goes silent—no warning, just wrong data. You’d have to manually check every alert before driving to be safe.  

For anyone building or publishing content around this: the tool is only as good as its weakest sensor, and that failure is invisible. 🛞  

So, ignore one tire alert on your next drive—will the assistant notice you skipped it, or just carry on like nothing happened? ⚠️🤖
